newsitem.title: UK: AMEC to divest 50 pct interest in BPMS.
newsitem.headline: AMEC to divest 50 pct interest in BPMS.

text.p: International engineering, construction and development Group AMEC Plc on Tuesday said it would sell its 50 percent interest in Building and Property Management Services Limited (BPMS) to a newly-formed company financed with funds arranged by CVC Capital Partners Limited.
AMEC said its Swiss-owned partner Pell Frischmann Facilities Management Limited had also agreed to sell its 50 percent stake in BPMS.
AMEC's share of the pre-sale dividend is 7.5 million stg and AMEC will, pursuant to the disposal, receive 27.5 million stg in cash on completion, the company said.
By 30 June 1998, AMEC will also receive 1.9 million stg by way of deferred consideration and may receive a further 1.4 million stg, the company said.

The total transaction is valued at 84.6 million stg, taking into account the retention by BPMS of 10.9 million stg of deferred consideration relating to the initial purchase of BPMS group companies from HM Government and a pre-sale dividend of 15.0 million stg.
The book value of AMEC's investment in BPMS at December 1995 was 169,000 stg, the company said. It described the whole sale transaction as "expected to be non-dilutive in 1997".
AMEC'S profit of 31.6 million stg, before goodwill written off, on the sale of its investment in BPMS is not anticipated to attract a tax liability, the company said.
